title: Psalms Chapter 89 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 89 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 89 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 89.

questions.question: Who is the author of Psalms 89?
questions.explanation: The chapter begins with the phrase 'Maschil of Ethan the Ezrahite', indicating Ethan as the author.

questions.question: What will the author sing of for ever?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'I will sing of the mercies of the LORD for ever'.

questions.question: True or False: The author will make known the faithfulness of the LORD to all generations.
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states, 'with my mouth will I make known thy faithfulness to all generations'.

questions.question: According to Psalms 89, what has God established in the very heavens?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 mentions that 'thy faithfulness shalt thou establish in the very heavens'.

questions.question: True or False: The author made a covenant with his chosen and swore unto David.
questions.explanation: Verse 3 states, 'I have made a covenant with my chosen, I have sworn unto David my servant'.

questions.question: What will God establish for ever according to Psalms 89:4?
questions.explanation: The verse declares, 'Thy seed will I establish for ever, and build up thy throne to all generations'.

questions.question: Who in heaven can be compared unto the LORD?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 poses the question, 'For who in the heaven can be compared unto the LORD?'.

questions.question: True or False: God is greatly to be feared in the assembly of the saints.
questions.explanation: Verse 7 states, 'God is greatly to be feared in the assembly of the saints'.

questions.question: What does verse 14 say are the habitation of God's throne?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne'.

questions.question: What is blessed according to Psalms 89:15?
options: The people that know the joyful sound
questions.correctAnswer: The people that know the joyful sound
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Blessed is the people that know the joyful sound'.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD is referred to as our defense in Psalms 89:18.
questions.explanation: Verse 18 states, 'For the LORD is our defence; and the Holy One of Israel is our king'.

questions.question: In Psalms 89, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: I will sing of the mercies of the LORD
Thy seed will I establish for ever
Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne
Thou hast broken Rahab in pieces
questions.correctAnswer: I will sing of the mercies of the LORD
questions.explanation: The very first declaration in the chapter is 'I will sing of the mercies of the LORD for ever'.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 89 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 89 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Psalms 89:20 say about David?
options: He was a servant of the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: He was a servant of the Lord
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:20 states, "I have found David my servant; with my holy oil have I anointed him," indicating that David is recognized as a servant of God.

questions.question: According to Psalms 89:22, what will not happen to David?
options: He will be afflicted by the wicked
He will be killed in battle
He will be abandoned by God
He will be prospered in all his ways
questions.correctAnswer: He will be afflicted by the wicked
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:22 says, "The enemy shall not exact upon him; nor the son of wickedness afflict him," signifying protection from evil.

questions.question: What is promised in Psalms 89:24 regarding David's relationship with God?
options: God's faithfulness and mercy will be with him
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness and mercy will be with him
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:24 states, "But my faithfulness and my mercy shall be with him," indicating God's ongoing support.

questions.question: In Psalms 89:26, what does David call God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:26 says, "He shall cry unto me, Thou art my father, my God, and the rock of my salvation," showing David's intimate relationship with God.

questions.question: What does Psalms 89:30 say will happen if David's children forsake God's law?
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:30 states, "If his children forsake my law, and walk not in my judgments;" implying that neglecting God's commandments leads to consequences.

questions.question: According to Psalms 89:33, what will not happen to David despite his sins?
options: God's lovingkindness will not be taken from him
He will cease to be king
questions.correctAnswer: God's lovingkindness will not be taken from him
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:33 states, "Nevertheless my lovingkindness will I not utterly take from him," showing God's enduring mercy.

questions.question: What does Psalms 89:35 affirm about God's promise to David?
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:35 states, "Once have I sworn by my holiness that I will not lie unto David," affirming God's faithfulness to His promise.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 89:31 states that if David's children break God's statutes, they will not be punished.
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:31 warns that if they break God's statutes, they will face consequences, indicating that disobedience has repercussions.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 89:41 describes David as a reproach to his neighbors.
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:41 states, "All that pass by the way spoil him: he is a reproach to his neighbours," indicating a loss of honor.

questions.question: How does Psalms 89:34 emphasize God's faithfulness?
options: He will not break His covenant
questions.correctAnswer: He will not break His covenant
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:34 states, "My covenant will I not break, nor alter the thing that is gone out of my lips," affirming God's unchanging nature.

questions.question: What is the significance of David being called God's firstborn in Psalms 89:27?
options: He will be like every other king
He is higher than the kings of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: He is higher than the kings of the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:27 states, "Also I will make him my firstborn, higher than the kings of the earth," indicating his special status.

questions.question: What does Psalms 89:19 highlight about God's communication with His chosen ones?
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:19 says, "Then thou spakest in vision to thy holy one," showing God's method of revealing His plans.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 89:46 questions how long God will remain hidden.
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:46 asks, "How long, LORD? wilt thou hide thyself for ever?" reflecting a plea for God's presence.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 89 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 89.

questions.question: What does Psalms 89:1 declare about the LORD's mercies?
options: They are only for a season
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:1 states, 'I will sing of the mercies of the LORD for ever,' indicating that the mercies of the LORD are eternal.

questions.question: Who is referred to as the 'anointed' in Psalms 89:38?
questions.explanation: In the context of the chapter, the 'anointed' refers to David, as the psalm reflects on God's covenant with him.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'my covenant shall stand fast with him' in Psalms 89:28 imply?
questions.explanation: This phrase indicates God's unwavering commitment to His covenant, suggesting its eternal nature.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Psalms 89:14 where justice and judgment are mentioned?
questions.explanation: The use of 'justice and judgment' reflects parallelism, a common literary device in Hebrew poetry that emphasizes related ideas.

questions.question: According to Psalms 89:39, what has been made void?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Thou hast made void the covenant of thy servant,' indicating a significant breach in God's promises to David.

questions.question: What does Psalms 89:43 indicate about David's situation in battle?
options: He has been turned from victory
questions.correctAnswer: He has been turned from victory
questions.explanation: The verse expresses that God has turned the edge of his sword, indicating a shift from victory to defeat.

questions.question: How long does the Psalmist question God's hiddenness in Psalms 89:46?
questions.explanation: The verse poses the question, 'How long, LORD? wilt thou hide thyself for ever?', emphasizing a desperate plea for God's presence.

questions.question: What does the 'horn' symbolize in Psalms 89:24?
questions.explanation: The term 'horn' symbolizes strength and power, indicating that David's strength will be exalted in the name of God.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 89:52 concludes the chapter with a blessing to the LORD.
questions.explanation: The chapter concludes with 'Blessed be the LORD for evermore. Amen, and Amen,' affirming a blessing to God.

questions.question: Which other passage emphasizes God's covenant with David, similar to Psalms 89:3?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:12-16 discusses God's promise to David, affirming the covenant he made with him, similar to Psalms 89:3.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'the days of his youth hast thou shortened' in Psalms 89:45?
questions.explanation: This phrase implies that David's suffering and the shortening of his days are consequences of his actions or the actions of his lineage.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 89:50 mentions the reproach of David's enemies.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Remember, Lord, the reproach of thy servants; how I do bear in my bosom the reproach of all the mighty people,' indicating the reproach faced by David.

questions.question: In the context of Psalms 89:37, which celestial body serves as a witness to the establishment of David's throne?
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:37 states, 'It shall be established for ever as the moon,' indicating that the moon serves as a faithful witness to God's promises.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 89 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 89 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 89:1 emphasize about the relationship between God's mercies and generations?
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:1 states, 'I will sing of the mercies of the LORD for ever,' highlighting the eternal nature of God's mercies.

questions.question: According to Psalms 89:3, with whom has God made a covenant?
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:3 states, 'I have made a covenant with my chosen, I have sworn unto David my servant,' indicating that the covenant is specifically with David.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Psalms 89:8?
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:8 refers to God's faithfulness when it asks, 'who is a strong LORD like unto thee? or to thy faithfulness round about thee?' demonstrating His attribute of faithfulness.

questions.question: How is God's power over nature illustrated in Psalms 89:9?
options: He rules the raging of the sea.
questions.correctAnswer: He rules the raging of the sea.
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:9 declares, 'Thou rulest the raging of the sea: when the waves thereof arise, thou stillest them,' illustrating God's sovereign control over nature.

questions.question: In Psalms 89:14, what two qualities are described as going before God's face?
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:14 states, 'Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne: mercy and truth shall go before thy face,' showing the attributes of mercy and truth.

questions.question: What promise does God make regarding David's throne in Psalms 89:29?
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:29 states, 'His seed also will I make to endure for ever, and his throne as the days of heaven,' promising the eternal nature of David's throne.

questions.question: According to Psalms 89:33, what will God not take from David?
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:33 assures, 'Nevertheless my lovingkindness will I not utterly take from him,' indicating God's enduring lovingkindness towards David.

questions.question: What is the significance of God being called 'the Holy One of Israel' in Psalms 89:18?
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:18 states, 'For the LORD is our defence; and the Holy One of Israel is our king,' emphasizing God's role as a defender.

questions.question: What did God say to His holy one in Psalms 89:19?
options: I will lay help upon one that is mighty.
questions.correctAnswer: I will lay help upon one that is mighty.
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:19 states, 'Then thou spakest in vision to thy holy one, and saidst, I have laid help upon one that is mighty,' indicating God's support for a powerful leader.

questions.question: What does Psalms 89:38 describe regarding God's relationship with His anointed?
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:38 states, 'But thou hast cast off and abhorred, thou hast been wroth with thine anointed,' indicating a moment of divine displeasure.

questions.question: What question does the psalmist pose in Psalms 89:46 regarding God's presence?
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:46 asks, 'How long, LORD? wilt thou hide thyself for ever?', expressing a longing for God's presence.

questions.question: What does Psalms 89:51 refer to in relation to God's enemies?
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:51 states, 'Wherewith thine enemies have reproached, O LORD; wherewith they have reproached the footsteps of thine anointed,' highlighting the mocking of God's enemies.

questions.question: How does Psalms 89:52 conclude the chapter?
options: With a declaration of God's glory.
With a blessing to the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: With a blessing to the LORD.
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:52 concludes with 'Blessed be the LORD for evermore. Amen, and Amen,' affirming eternal praise to God.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's faithfulness is unreliable. What does Psalms 89:33-34 actually teach?
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:33-34 teaches that 'Nevertheless my lovingkindness will I not utterly take from him, nor suffer my faithfulness to fail. My covenant will I not break,' affirming God's unwavering faithfulness to His covenant.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Psalms 89:27 and 89:29 convey about God's relationship with David?
options: He is David's father and sees his seed endure.
He will not bless David's throne.
questions.correctAnswer: He is David's father and sees his seed endure.
questions.explanation: Psalms 89:27 states that God will make David His firstborn, and verse 29 promises that his seed will endure forever, emphasizing a father-son relationship and the lasting nature of David's lineage.
